description: US-listed companies by market cap, largest first (dir=asc for smallest first), optionally within min_market_cap_usd and max_market_cap_usd (US dollars, both inclusive; give either, both or neither). For companies around $100 million, try for example min_market_cap_usd 50000000 and max_market_cap_usd 200000000. Market cap is the latest daily closing price of the company's primary ticker times the shares outstanding on its latest SEC 10-K or 10-Q cover page (shares_as_of), adjusted for stock splits since then (split_factor, 1 = none). It is recalculated every US trading day after the close; close_date is the trading day of the close used. No stock price is returned. Companies without a market cap are not listed: no_price or stale_price (no daily close in the last 7 days, for example OTC or halted stocks), no_shares or stale_shares (no cover-page share count within about 400 days, common for companies whose cover lists several share classes separately, such as GOOGL/GOOG, BRK or META), foreign_filer (a Form 20-F filer: the US listing is usually ADSs and the ADS ratio is not in SEC data), shares_mismatch (the cover-page share count does not match the listed shares: 13F institutions report holding more than 1.5 times the cover-page shares, which points to several share classes or ADSs, or the company has two or more traded common lines whose latest closes differ by more than 1.25 times, such as multi-fund ETP trusts like ProShares Trust II that share one cover-page share count) or out_of_range (an implausible value, including a market cap below $1 million). So Form 20-F issuers whose US shares are ADSs, companies whose cover page lists several share classes and multi-fund ETP trusts are missing. One row per company: ticker (the priced ticker), name, exchange, SIC industry, market_cap_usd, close_date, shares, shares_as_of, split_factor and url (the stock page). total counts every matching company and as_of is the newest close date. To research a company, follow up with get_stock, get_financials and get_insider_trades. At most 200 rows per call; use page.

dir.description: desc = largest market cap first (default); asc = smallest first.

max_market_cap_usd.description: Largest market cap in US dollars, inclusive; not below min_market_cap_usd. Default: no maximum.

min_market_cap_usd.description: Smallest market cap in US dollars, inclusive (100000000 = $100 million). Default: no minimum.

page.description: Page number starting at 1; each page has `limit` rows. Check has_more.

name: screen_stocks

as_of.description: The newest close date in the market cap data; null before it is loaded.

ticker.description: The priced ticker (the company's primary ticker).

total.description: Number of companies matching the range (all pages).

title: Screen companies by market cap
